title: Anthropic Discloses Post-IPO Equity Details; Amazon and Google to Hold Nearly 30% Combined

content_html:
On Tuesday, November 17, Anthropic disclosed details of its largest investment agreements with its core cloud service providers Amazon and Google, specifying that after the initial public offering, Amazon and Google will hold 14.7% and 13.7% stakes in it, respectively, totaling nearly 30%.

Between 2023 and 2024 (before Claude Code swept the enterprise world and while Anthropic was still under OpenAI's shadow), Amazon invested billions of dollars to obtain convertible promissory notes, with conversion prices of approximately $2.09 or $5.05 per share. At the IPO, Amazon will convert some of the bonds into special non-voting shares that are entitled to dividends and can be converted into Class A voting shares upon sale, giving it a 14.7% stake; if all remaining billions of dollars in bonds are converted, its stake could reach 23.8%. In addition, Anthropic has committed to spending more than $100 billion on AWS cloud services over the next decade.

Google's 13.7% stake is also in non-voting shares, arising from bond conversion and a concurrent private placement at the IPO. Tech giants including AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia, and TSMC have agreed to subscribe to $26 billion of such non-voting shares, with Google and Nvidia each subscribing $10 billion.

Cloud providers and chip giants are deeply participating in the capital and compute binding of leading AI companies through convertible bonds and IPO private placements, reflecting the strategic logic of infrastructure giants using equity collaboration to consolidate the AI ecosystem and long-term compute demand.
